message:
feat(host): give an unresponsive window a budget instead of unlimited patience

Product 1 (new header), test 1, build 1. Nothing calls it yet -- the host still has no
deadline, so this changes no behaviour. Wiring it in is the step that is still waiting on a
decision, and until then this is policy sitting next to the problem rather than fixing it.

On 2026-09-15 a window stopped answering WM_PRINT and the control dispatcher sat inside
PrintWindow for 1h50m. Every session on that host failed for the duration, because the
dispatcher is one per process and could not get back to reading. A deadline alone would have
saved the session and then paid that deadline again on the very next request, forever. So
the deadline needs something that remembers: three tries, then skip the window for a minute,
and one success wipes the record.

The key is (HWND, owner pid, process creation time). Two of those exist because the first is
not enough -- HWND values and pids are both recycled, and the creation time is what stops a
new process on an old pid from inheriting the punishment. What it cannot do is separate a
window from its replacement inside one live process: all three fields are identical there.
That is stated on the type rather than papered over, and it is handled from outside, by
dropping entries for windows that leave the list. The residual error is one window skipped
for at most one cooldown -- it lands on "no preview for a minute", not "session stuck".

No Win32 and no clock of its own: identity arrives as integers, time is an argument. That is
what lets the sixty second cooldown be a number in the test instead of a minute of runtime,
and it is why the policy could be settled before the capture mechanism was.

39 checks pass. They also fail when they should: removing the cooldown breaks 12 of them,
charging a cancelled attempt against the budget breaks 3, and letting a success leave a
running cooldown in place breaks 2. A suite that passes against a broken policy would have
been decoration.

Two of those checks started out wrong and are worth naming, because both were the test
lying in the comfortable direction: the helper advanced the clock one interval past the last
attempt and then measured the cooldown from there, and another asserted a cooldown after a
single timeout when the budget is three.
